description: This iconic American soup features tender clams, diced potatoes, crispy bacon, and a rich, creamy broth. Perfect for a chilly day, it delivers a comforting taste of the New England coast right to your table. Enjoy this hearty and flavorful classic that is a staple in American cuisine.

instructions.title: Cook the Bacon
instructions.text: In a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, cook the diced bacon over medium heat until crispy. Remove the bacon with a slotted spoon, reserving about 2 tablespoons of bacon fat in the pot. Set the crispy bacon aside for garnish.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics
instructions.text: Add the diced onion and celery to the reserved bacon fat in the pot. Sauté over medium heat until the vegetables are softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Do not brown them.

instructions.title: Simmer Potatoes
instructions.text: Add the diced potatoes, clam juice, and the reserved liquid from the canned clams to the pot. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and cook until the potatoes are tender, about 15-20 minutes. Do not drain the liquid.

instructions.title: Prepare the Roux
instructions.text: While the potatoes are simmering, melt the butter in a separate small saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to create a smooth roux. This will be the thickening agent for your chowder.

instructions.title: Thicken the Chowder
instructions.text: Gradually whisk the warm heavy cream and whole milk into the roux until smooth. Pour this cream mixture into the pot with the simmering potatoes and clam juice. Stir well to combine. Continue to simmer gently, stirring occasionally, until the chowder thickens to your desired consistency, about 5-7 minutes. Do not bring to a rolling boil.

instructions.title: Add Clams and Season
instructions.text: Stir in the drained chopped clams and heat through for just 1-2 minutes; overcooking will make them tough. Season the chowder with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste. Ladle the hot chowder into bowls, garnish with the reserved crispy bacon and fresh chopped parsley.

tips: For extra depth of flavor, use fresh clams and steam them yourself, reserving the delicious clam liquor to replace some of the bottled clam juice.
Do not boil the chowder once the cream and milk are added; a gentle simmer is best to prevent curdling and maintain a smooth, rich texture.
Serve your clam chowder with classic oyster crackers on the side and a sprinkle of fresh parsley or chives for an authentic New England experience.
